source: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 20 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 20
knowledgePattern: Use derivative-root multiplicities to bound and construct stationary types
solution:
The derivative is a polynomial of degree 6. A local maximum or minimum needs a sign-changing derivative root, of odd multiplicity at least 1. A zero-gradient inflection needs a derivative root with no sign change, of even multiplicity at least 2.

Therefore, if the proposed numbers of minima, maxima and zero-gradient inflections are m, n and s, they must satisfy m+n+2s≤6. This excludes A, B, D and E.

The derivative has the same sign at both far ends because its degree is even. As we move from left to right, its sign-changing roots alternate between a change from positive to negative and a change from negative to positive. It must therefore have equal numbers of maxima and minima. This excludes C and F.

G is attainable: choose y′=(x+2)(x+1)x(x−1)(x−2)2. There are four simple roots, producing two maxima and two minima, and a double root at 2, producing a zero-gradient inflection. Integrating this degree-six polynomial gives a degree-seven polynomial with nonzero leading coefficient.

Thus the possible triple is (2,2,1). Answer G.

hints.title: Look at the derivative
hints.body: Differentiate just the highest-power term first. What degree must the derivative have? Every point counted in the question needs a zero of this derivative.
hints.recap: Stationary points are found where the derivative is zero.
hints.pitfall: Count zeros of the derivative, not zeros of the original polynomial.

recall.reminder: Stationary points are found where the derivative is zero.

hints.title: Compare crossing with touching
hints.body: The factor x−r changes sign at r; (x−r)2 does not. Use this to work out the fewest factors needed for a maximum, a minimum and a zero-gradient inflection.
hints.recap: An odd power changes sign across its root; an even power does not.
hints.pitfall: A repeated root is one location but uses more than one factor.
hints.pause: Check which proposed triples already need too high a degree.

recall.reminder: An odd power changes sign across its root; an even power does not.

hints.title: Check the signs at both far ends
hints.body: Use the derivative’s leading term to compare its signs far to the left and far to the right. Sketch the sign changes as you pass each maximum and minimum.
hints.recap: A maximum changes the derivative from positive to negative; a minimum does the reverse.
hints.pitfall: Passing the degree check alone does not show that a triple is possible.
hints.pause: Check the remaining triples, then write factors for a derivative that realises your choice.

recall.reminder: A maximum changes the derivative from positive to negative; a minimum does the reverse.
